kicker.zh: FATE / AI 轉型工作記錄

title.en: Making AI part of how work gets done.
title.zh: 讓 AI 融入工作的方式。

lede.en: I am Fate, a product leader putting AI to work. My journey runs from personal knowledge to departmental change and company-wide transformation.
lede.zh: 我是 Fate，一名把 AI 帶入實際工作的產品負責人。從個人知識庫出發，我逐步改造部門的工作方式，並推動公司層面的 AI 轉型。

journey_title.en: From my knowledge base to AI work across the company.
journey_title.zh: 從個人知識庫，到部門和公司的 AI 轉型。

text.en: Organize my materials, preserve context, and let AI work with accumulated knowledge.
text.zh: 從整理自己的材料開始，保存背景，讓 AI 能在積累的知識上工作。

text.en: Rebuild how my department tracks work, produces analysis, shares results, and hands work over.
text.zh: 改造所管理部門的進展跟進、分析、成果共享與工作交接方式。

text.en: Bring these lessons to other departments. The goal is an AI Native company, with transformation still underway.
text.zh: 開始把經驗複製到各部門。目標是成為 AI Native 公司，轉型仍在推進中。

updates_heading.zh: 記錄每一次迭代的過程。

updates_description.en: Follow the work by date: what we did, what changed, and why.
updates_description.zh: 從知識庫整理、部門管理到公司轉型，按日期記下做了什麼、改了什麼，以及為什麼改。

principle.zh: 人和 AI 應該有清晰的合作邊界，合理的分工才能推動公司業務增長，而不僅僅是提高個人效率。
principle.en: People and AI need clear boundaries for collaboration. A sensible division of responsibilities drives company growth, beyond individual productivity.

title.zh: AI 具體幫我們做了什麼。

lede.zh: 從部門管理、客服到調研與 AI 中台，九個案例介紹我們怎樣把工作交給 AI。
lede.en: Nine cases explain how we use AI in departmental management, support, research, and a shared work platform.

kicker.zh: 案例 01 / AI 工作體系

title.zh: 實現部門工作管理自動化。

lede.en: AI connects a shared work baseline, new evidence, progress review, and clarification to support departmental coordination.
lede.zh: 把分散的工作信息連成可持續更新的體系，支持團隊協作與管理判斷。

title.zh: 要解決的問題與已有成果

paragraphs.en: Work information was scattered across records and conversations. Reviewing progress required people to assemble the context again.
paragraphs.zh: 工作信息分散在記錄與溝通中，每次回顧進展都需要重新拼湊背景。

paragraphs.en: A shared work list, progress overview, and focused clarification now support departmental coordination.
paragraphs.zh: 共同工作清單、進展概覽與針對性確認，已用於部門日常協調。

title.zh: 先確認一份工作項基線

paragraphs.en: AI first assembled candidate work items from existing records. We reviewed them together, merging overlaps and removing unsuitable entries.
paragraphs.zh: AI 先從已有記錄整理候選工作項，再由大家一起過，合併重複、刪去不適合作為工作項的內容。

paragraphs.en: The baseline records the purpose, owner, priority, expected outcome, and relevant timing of each item.
paragraphs.zh: 基線說清每項工作的目的、負責人、優先順序、預期結果與相關時間要求。

paragraphs.en: People confirmed that starting point. Subsequent updates refer back to it, rather than creating another disconnected list.
paragraphs.zh: 這個起點由人確認，後續更新回到同一份清單，而不是不斷另建互不相通的列表。

paragraphs.en: Inputs include meeting records, work communications, project records, and completed work. Records are read directly or provided through exports.
paragraphs.zh: 輸入包括會議記錄、工作溝通、項目記錄與已完成成果，透過直接讀取或導出材料取得。

paragraphs.en: AI matches new evidence to existing items, summarizes progress and blockers, and retains the supporting context.
paragraphs.zh: AI 把新證據歸到既有工作項，整理進展與卡點，保留支撐判斷的背景。

paragraphs.en: People review new work and conflicting information before changing the shared list.
paragraphs.zh: 遇到新工作或互相衝突的信息，先核對，再更新共同清單。

title.en: Make the same information useful to different readers
title.zh: 讓不同的人讀同一套工作事實

paragraphs.en: The work list preserves item-level detail. The overview highlights changes, questions, and decisions needing attention.
paragraphs.zh: 工作清單保留逐項細節，概覽則突出變化、問題與需要關注的決策。

paragraphs.en: Department members check their work and dependencies. The manager reviews priorities, coordination, and issues requiring a decision.
paragraphs.zh: 部門成員查看自己的工作與協作依賴，管理者查看優先順序、協調問題與待決策事項。

paragraphs.en: The dashboard gives everyone a quick view; the work list provides the detail needed for follow-up.
paragraphs.zh: 看板方便大家快速查看，工作清單則提供跟進時需要的細節。

title.en: Ask about a specific problem, then update the record
title.zh: 圍繞具體問題確認，再回到工作記錄

paragraphs.en: When an item needs clarification, AI prepares a focused question using the known facts and asks with the relevant colleagues.
paragraphs.zh: 某個工作項需要澄清時，AI 結合已知事實提出具體問題，向相關同事確認。

paragraphs.en: Confirmed answers become evidence for the next update. Commitments and material changes remain subject to human decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 有效確認成為下一次更新的證據；承諾與重大調整仍由人決定。

paragraphs.en: Routine checks stay quiet when nothing needs action. Questions and answers remain attached to the relevant work item.
paragraphs.zh: 例行檢查沒有需要行動的變化時保持安靜，問題與答覆留在對應工作項中，方便繼續跟進。

paragraphs.en: I confirmed the baseline, defined judgment and escalation rules, and review important decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 我確認工作基線，定義進展判讀和升級處理的規則，並審閱重要決策。

paragraphs.en: The dashboard is one view of the work. The shared record and human decisions keep it useful.
paragraphs.zh: 看板只是呈現方式；共同工作記錄與人的判斷，讓它能繼續服務實際工作。

kicker.zh: 案例 02 / AI 工作體系

title.en: Let AI assess partners. Let people move cooperation forward.
title.zh: 讓 AI 持續評估伙伴，讓人專注推動合作。

lede.en: One framework covers 126 partners across every stage. AI maintains assessments; people focus on moving cooperation forward.
lede.zh: 一套跨領域框架，納入全部階段的 126 家伙伴。AI 持續更新評估，人專注推動合作。

title.zh: 既要推動合作，又要記住所有細節

paragraphs.en: Partner information keeps changing across conversations and documents. People had to advance discussions while maintaining every assessment.
paragraphs.zh: 伙伴跨越不同領域，反饋與材料持續變化。同事既要推動溝通，又要記住細節、整理證據和更新判斷，容易出現遺漏與延遲。

title.en: Define a framework that travels across fields
title.zh: 先把跨領域的評估標準定清楚

paragraphs.en: I defined a shared framework with eight dimensions and 24 research items. Each field uses relevant evidence and comparisons.
paragraphs.zh: 我制訂了八個維度、24 項研究內容的統一框架。不同領域沿用共同的判斷結構，再按具體業務選擇證據與比較指標。

paragraphs.en: Assessments connect conclusions to evidence, conditions, and unresolved questions. A single score cannot replace these judgments.
paragraphs.zh: 評估保留結論、依據、適用條件與待確認問題，讓人看清為什麼值得推進、哪些條件會改變判斷，而不是依賴一個總分。

title.zh: 讓 AI 持續承擔評估更新

paragraphs.en: The framework now runs in our shared AI platform. AI checks connected sources daily for new feedback and materials.
paragraphs.zh: 這套工作已遷入 AI 中台，每天自動運轉。已接入的多種來源出現新的反饋或材料後，AI 整理證據並接回已有評估。

paragraphs.en: It updates affected judgments, preserves useful history, and identifies questions that could change the next decision.
paragraphs.zh: AI 更新受影響的判斷、保留有效歷史，並提出會影響下一步決定的關鍵問題。日常評估維護由 AI 承擔，同事不必重新拼湊整套材料。

title.en: People focus on moving cooperation forward
title.zh: 人把精力放回推動合作

paragraphs.en: Colleagues advance conversations, obtain useful feedback, and coordinate the next step. People decide priorities, trade-offs, and commitments.
paragraphs.zh: 同事專注推動溝通、取得關鍵反饋、協調資源和促成下一步。優先順序、重要取捨與對外承諾，仍由人決定。

paragraphs.en: New information from connected sources feeds the next assessment update. The work continues from accumulated knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 只要持續推動事情、讓新的材料進入已接入來源，AI 就能接續更新評估。每次溝通都能在已有知識上繼續前進。

title.en: My contribution and the change it enabled
title.zh: 我做的改變，與它帶來的價值

paragraphs.en: I defined the framework, clarified responsibilities, and moved recurring assessment work onto the shared AI platform.
paragraphs.zh: 我的投入是定義評估框架、劃清人與 AI 的職責，並推動這項工作從人工維護轉為中台持續運行。

paragraphs.en: AI carries the ongoing assessment work. People spend more attention on relationships, decisions, and actions that advance cooperation.
paragraphs.zh: 評估工作的持續整理與更新由 AI 接手，人把更多注意力放在關係、判斷與行動上。AI 和人各自做好擅長的工作，才是我希望形成的工作狀態。

image_alt.en: Partner assessment workspace and shared research framework
image_alt.zh: 伙伴評估研究室與統一研究框架

scope.en: All stages: initial research, evaluation, active cooperation, paused, declined, and exited. Counted on November 18, 2026.
scope.zh: 涵蓋待了解、評估中、合作中、暫停觀察、決定不合作及歷史退出等全部階段。統計日期：2026-11-18。

kicker.zh: 案例 03 / AI 工作體系

title.en: Let AI test what products can actually do.
title.zh: 讓 AI 走進真實產品流程，核對功能到底能不能用。

lede.en: People define the question. AI checks real product flows, compares evidence, and builds a reviewable assessment.
lede.zh: 人提出業務問題，AI 操作真實產品流程、核對資料並保存證據，再由人判斷對產品有什麼影響。

title.zh: 從真實的產品問題開始

paragraphs.en: A shared framework defines the research scope. We ask what users can accomplish, what conditions apply, and where difficulties arise.
paragraphs.zh: 共同框架定義調研範圍。先問用戶能完成什麼、需要哪些條件、會在哪裡遇到困難，再決定查什麼資料、測哪些流程。

title.en: Move from documentation to product use
title.zh: 從查資料，走到實際操作

paragraphs.en: AI operates a mobile app on a real device, checking receiving flows, swap quotes, minimum amounts, and error recovery.
paragraphs.zh: AI 在真實手機上操作 App，檢查收款流程、兌換報價、最低額、限制提示與異常恢復。

paragraphs.en: Recent research tested accessible flows without funds. Screenshots record the observed behavior alongside official documentation.
paragraphs.zh: 近期研究已完成無資金條件下可操作流程的檢查，保存實測截圖，並與官方說明逐項對照。

paragraphs.en: A listed feature becomes a concrete question: can users reach it, obtain a quote, and understand the next step?
paragraphs.zh: 功能清單上的一項能力，會變成具體問題：用戶能否找到入口、取得報價，並理解下一步怎麼做？

title.zh: 把發現整理成可比較的證據

paragraphs.en: Reports distinguish observed behavior, documented facts, vendor claims, and untested steps. Consistent dimensions support comparison across products.
paragraphs.zh: 報告區分實際操作、文件事實、廠商主張與未測步驟，按一致維度整理，方便跨產品比較。

paragraphs.en: When a product changes, AI checks affected evidence and updates the findings while retaining relevant history.
paragraphs.zh: 產品變化後，AI 核對受影響的證據並更新發現；仍然有效的歷史材料繼續保留，不必每次從頭調研。

paragraphs.en: Product reports and screenshots show the difference between advertised capability and accessible experience. People decide which differences matter.
paragraphs.zh: 已有調研報告和實測截圖，呈現宣傳能力與實際體驗之間的差異。人判斷哪些差異影響用戶，哪些值得繼續深挖。

paragraphs.en: I define the business questions and comparison standards. AI gathers evidence; colleagues and I evaluate its implications for product decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 我定義業務問題與比較標準；AI 負責操作、取材與整理，我和相關同事判斷其產品意義，決定是否採納建議。

kicker.zh: 案例 04 / AI 工作體系

title.en: Produce external material from shared facts and standards.
title.zh: 讓 AI 依據統一事實與標準製作對外材料。

lede.en: Connect accumulated knowledge, audience requirements, terminology, and review to produce consistent material in different formats.
lede.zh: 把積累的知識、受眾要求、術語及審閱連起來，形成不同格式、口徑一致的對外材料。

title.en: A shared basis for different outputs
title.zh: 不同產出，共用同一份依據

paragraphs.en: Copy, presentations, and formal documents should not each invent their own company facts, terminology, or product descriptions.
paragraphs.zh: 文案、演講與正式文書，不應各自另造一套公司事實、術語或產品描述。

paragraphs.en: We provide the audience, purpose, constraints, and applicable facts. AI retrieves relevant knowledge and prepares a draft against those standards.
paragraphs.zh: 先明確受眾、目的、限制與適用事實，再由 AI 取用相關知識，依標準準備初稿。

title.en: From content to a reviewable artifact
title.zh: 從內容，到可以審閱的成品

paragraphs.en: AI can develop an outline, draft copy, assemble slides, and check terminology or layout. People review meaning, emphasis, and publication.
paragraphs.zh: AI 可協助形成提綱、撰寫文案、組成幻燈片並檢查術語或版式；人審閱含義、重點與發佈。

paragraphs.en: Quotations link to meeting records, and company facts follow the shared reference material.
paragraphs.zh: 發言引文附會議來源，公司與產品事實沿用共同資料。

paragraphs.en: The work has produced English copy, presentation versions, and other formal material, with reusable facts and language standards.
paragraphs.zh: 已形成英文文案、演講版本及其他正式材料，並積累可複用的事實與語言標準。

paragraphs.en: I provide the message, judgments, and audience priorities. AI helps research, structure, draft, format, and check the material.
paragraphs.zh: 我提供觀點、判斷與受眾重點；AI 協助取材、組織、起草、排版與檢查。

kicker.zh: 案例 05 / AI 工作體系

title.en: Use AI to organize reviews, coverage, and impersonation reports.
title.zh: 用 AI 整理用戶評價、報道與仿冒線索。

lede.en: AI-assisted collection, classification, deduplication, and evidence records turn scattered feedback into a reviewable report.
lede.zh: 透過 AI 輔助採集、分類、去重與證據記錄，把分散反饋轉成可審閱的報告。

paragraphs.en: Reviews and coverage are scattered across public sources. Reading them individually makes comparisons and historical follow-up difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 評價與報道散落在不同公開來源，逐條閱讀不利於比較，也難以追蹤歷史。

paragraphs.en: AI helps collect accessible material, distinguish topics and sentiment, remove duplicates, and retain references for review.
paragraphs.zh: AI 協助採集可取得的內容、辨認主題與情感、去除重複，並保留可核對的來源。

paragraphs.en: Reports separate new feedback, historical context, and leads that need follow-up.
paragraphs.zh: 報告分別整理新增反饋、歷史背景與需要跟進的線索。

paragraphs.en: For suspected impersonation, AI helps organize public evidence and prepare communication drafts. People verify the concern and decide the response.
paragraphs.zh: 對疑似仿冒線索，AI 協助整理公開證據並準備溝通草稿，由人核實問題、決定如何處置。

paragraphs.en: The practice produced archived reports and accumulated feedback records. These support communication review and issues requiring further investigation.
paragraphs.zh: 這項實踐已形成歷史報告與累積反饋記錄，支撐溝通審閱及待進一步核查的問題。

paragraphs.en: People review important findings and decide what communication or follow-up is needed.
paragraphs.zh: 人審閱重要發現，決定需要哪些溝通與後續處理。

paragraphs.en: I set the reporting questions and quality requirements. Colleagues handle business follow-up; AI supports collection, interpretation, and drafting.
paragraphs.zh: 我確定觀察問題與品質要求，同事推進具體業務處理；AI 參與採集、判讀與起草。

kicker.zh: 案例 06 / AI 工作體系

title.en: Use AI to build and revise financial models.
title.zh: 讓 AI 參與財務模型的建立與修訂。

lede.en: Connect authoritative inputs, explicit assumptions, calculation, reconciliation, and human review rather than generating an isolated forecast.
lede.zh: 把權威輸入、明確假設、計算、對賬與人工審閱連起來，而不是只生成一份孤立預測。

title.en: Give the model a grounded starting point

paragraphs.en: We define periods, metric meanings, actual inputs, and assumptions before building the model.
paragraphs.zh: 先明確期間、指標含義、實際輸入與假設，再建立模型。

paragraphs.en: AI helps organize inputs, construct scenario models, trace calculation dependencies, and revise the model when assumptions or confirmed inputs change.
paragraphs.zh: AI 協助整理輸入、建立情景模型、檢查計算依賴，並隨假設或已確認輸入變化修訂模型。

paragraphs.en: Reconciliation and historical comparisons test whether the model behaves plausibly. A desired result is not a reason to change assumptions.
paragraphs.zh: 對賬與歷史比較用來檢查模型是否合理；想得到某個結果，不能成為改假設的理由。

paragraphs.en: The work produced models, scenario summaries, and review records. Saved assumptions make later revisions easier.
paragraphs.zh: 已形成模型、情景摘要與審閱記錄，保留假設，方便後續調整再計算。

paragraphs.en: I define the business questions and challenge assumptions. AI assists modelling; finance and relevant owners verify their source inputs.
paragraphs.zh: 我定義業務問題並挑戰假設；AI 協助建模，財務及相關資料負責人核對各自輸入。

kicker.zh: 案例 07 / AI 工作體系

title.en: From manual customer support to automation.
title.zh: 人工客服向自動化的轉變。

lede.en: AI supports replies. Structured case records can also help improve future support and products.
lede.zh: AI 協助處理客服問題，沉澱下來的個案資料與經驗，也能用於後續服務和產品改進。

title.zh: 要解決的問題與已有成果

paragraphs.en: Support involved reading each conversation, finding relevant knowledge, and preparing a reply. Useful experience was hard to reuse.
paragraphs.zh: 客服需要逐封理解問題、查找知識並組織回覆，處理過的經驗也不容易再次使用。

paragraphs.en: Reply assistance, structured case knowledge, and support reports now provide a foundation for follow-up.
paragraphs.zh: 已形成回覆輔助、結構化個案知識與客服報告，為後續工作提供基礎。

title.en: From reading every message to reviewing a draft
title.zh: 從逐封處理，到確認 AI 準備的回覆

paragraphs.en: Previously, a support colleague read the conversation, checked product knowledge, found similar cases, and wrote the reply.
paragraphs.zh: 原來需要客服逐封讀取往來、查產品知識、找相似案例，再組織回覆。

paragraphs.en: AI now helps classify the issue, use relevant knowledge and earlier conversations, and prepare a draft.
paragraphs.zh: 現在由 AI 協助分類問題，結合相關知識與歷史往來，先準備回覆草稿。

paragraphs.en: The support colleague reviews the draft, adds case-specific judgment, and confirms sending. Corrections improve the material used next time.
paragraphs.zh: 客服同事審閱草稿，補充具體個案的判斷並確認發送；糾正過的內容留作下一次處理的參考。

title.en: Turn each case into usable data
title.zh: 讓每張工單留下可分析的數據

paragraphs.en: We organize the question, product context, category, handling history, and reply activity into structured case records.
paragraphs.zh: 把問題、產品背景、分類、處理過程及回覆情況整理為結構化個案記錄。

paragraphs.en: AI reads these records to prepare reports on new issues, recurring topics, response activity, and questions still awaiting follow-up.
paragraphs.zh: AI 根據這些記錄形成報告，整理新增問題、反覆出現的主題、回覆情況與仍需跟進的事項。

paragraphs.en: Managers can compare periods and topics instead of reading every ticket again.
paragraphs.zh: 管理者可以按時段和主題比較，不必為每次統計重新讀完所有工單。

title.en: Use the experience in future support
title.zh: 把處理經驗用在下一次服務

paragraphs.en: Past cases help AI find similar questions and prepare more relevant replies.
paragraphs.zh: 遇到相似問題時，AI 可以查找既有案例，準備更貼合問題的回覆。

paragraphs.en: Repeated explanations can inform help articles, reply templates, and onboarding material for colleagues.
paragraphs.zh: 反覆需要解釋的問題，可以整理為幫助文章、回覆模板與同事的培訓材料。

paragraphs.en: Corrections and effective solutions provide concrete examples for improving the support knowledge base.
paragraphs.zh: 被糾正的理解和有效處理方法，則成為完善客服知識庫的具體例子。

title.en: Use support evidence to improve products
title.zh: 把客服數據用於產品改進

paragraphs.en: Grouped feedback shows which questions recur, which product areas cause confusion, and which issues deserve further investigation.
paragraphs.zh: 按主題歸納反饋，可以看見哪些問題反覆出現、哪些功能讓用戶困惑，以及哪些事項值得進一步排查。

paragraphs.en: Product colleagues can use this evidence to prioritize investigation and improve instructions, interaction design, and support content.
paragraphs.zh: 產品同事可據此安排排查的優先順序，改進操作說明、交互設計與幫助內容。

paragraphs.en: The same records support later comparisons after a change, making customer support useful beyond the individual reply.
paragraphs.zh: 改進後仍可用同一套記錄做前後比較，讓客服的價值從回覆一封郵件，延伸到改善產品。

paragraphs.en: I define the management questions and reporting standards. Support colleagues contribute service experience; AI assists with preparation and organization.
paragraphs.zh: 我定義管理問題與報告標準；客服同事提供服務經驗，AI 協助處理與整理。

kicker.zh: 案例 08 / AI 工作體系

title.en: Write clear instructions and let AI do the work.
title.zh: 把工作寫清楚，交給 AI 執行。

lede.en: Define the goal, materials, steps, and checks so AI can execute the task and others can take it over.
lede.zh: 把工作的目標、材料、步驟和檢查標準寫清楚，交給 AI 執行，也方便其他人接手。

title.en: Define the work before handing it over
title.zh: 先定義工作，再交給 AI

paragraphs.en: We specify the purpose, intended users, required inputs, quality standards, outputs, and acceptance conditions for recurring work.
paragraphs.zh: 先說清重複工作的目的、使用人、必要輸入、品質標準、輸出與驗收條件。

paragraphs.en: AI and supporting programs then follow those definitions. Review responsibilities and consequential decisions remain explicit.
paragraphs.zh: AI 與配套程序據此執行，審閱責任和重要決策要求一併明確。

paragraphs.en: A work instruction also explains ownership, verification, and recovery, so another person or AI can continue the work.
paragraphs.zh: 工作說明書還要交代誰負責、怎樣算完成、遇到問題如何接續，讓另一個人或 AI 讀完後能繼續做。

title.en: Keep the instruction tied to execution
title.zh: 讓說明書跟著實際工作變化

paragraphs.en: The instruction includes the supporting rules and materials. When the work changes, the description must change with it.
paragraphs.zh: 說明書連同配套規則與材料一起維護，工作變了，說明也要跟著變。

paragraphs.en: Execution records and feedback show what needs changing in the instruction.
paragraphs.zh: 從執行記錄與使用反饋中找出問題，再修改工作說明書。

title.en: Carry the work beyond its first operator
title.zh: 讓個人跑通的工作可以交接

paragraphs.en: The handover includes current standards, useful history, unfinished work, and checks against real outputs.
paragraphs.zh: 交接時一併保留現行標準、有效歷史、未完成事項及實際成果的檢查方式，讓接手者知道工作做到哪裡。

paragraphs.en: Support reporting and partner assessment now run on the shared AI platform. Their instructions preserve how the work should continue.
paragraphs.zh: 客服工單日報與伙伴評估已交由 AI 中台運行，工作說明書讓已驗證的做法能被持續使用，而不只留在最初執行者的經驗裡。

title.en: Give different tasks a shared factual basis
title.zh: 讓不同 AI 工作使用同一套事實

paragraphs.en: We established shared sources for important business facts. Research and reports refer to the same current records.
paragraphs.zh: 我們為重要業務事實建立共同來源，讓研究、報告與協作引用同一套現行記錄。

paragraphs.en: New information is checked for scope and version before updates. Shared records have been synchronized and checked against their sources.
paragraphs.zh: 新資料先核對口徑與版本，再更新共同記錄；已完成共享入口、版本同步與來源核對。

paragraphs.en: Work instructions specify which sources to use, helping different AI tasks continue from consistent facts.
paragraphs.zh: 工作說明書明確指定該引用哪些來源，讓不同 AI 任務接續時有一致的事實基礎。

paragraphs.en: Work instructions, supporting materials, and handover checks now support recurring work beyond its original operator.
paragraphs.zh: 工作說明書、配套材料與交接檢查已用於重複工作，將個人驗證過的做法接續為團隊可使用的能力。

paragraphs.en: I define standards and acceptance boundaries. AI prepares the instruction, reusable materials, and checks against the defined requirements.
paragraphs.zh: 我定義標準與驗收邊界；AI 協助形成說明書、可複用材料，並依要求檢查。

title.zh: 我對 AI 轉型的判斷。

lede.en: How to start, divide the work, and judge whether AI is helping.
lede.zh: 怎樣推動轉型、怎樣分工，以及怎樣判斷 AI 的工作有沒有用。

title.en: Buying AI tools is not transformation.

lede.en: Transformation begins when the way work is organized changes.
lede.zh: 轉型從工作組織方式的改變開始。

paragraphs.en: A tool can help one person finish faster while leaving everyone else working in the old way.
paragraphs.zh: 工具可以讓一個人做得更快，其他人卻仍按照舊方式工作。

paragraphs.en: That improvement matters, but it does not automatically become organizational capability.
paragraphs.zh: 這種改善有價值，但不會自動變成組織能力。

paragraphs.en: Who defines the result? How is work reviewed? Can useful knowledge survive the person who first produced it?
paragraphs.zh: 誰來定義結果？工作如何審閱？有用的知識能不能離開最初產出它的人而繼續存在？

paragraphs.en: These questions turn AI adoption into a management problem, rather than a shopping list.
paragraphs.zh: 這些問題，會把 AI 採用變成管理問題，而不只是採購清單。

paragraphs.en: I look for changes in responsibilities, shared standards, and how results reach the next person.
paragraphs.zh: 我會看責任、共同標準，以及成果如何到達下一個人，是否發生改變。

paragraphs.en: The question is whether better work becomes easier to repeat across the organization.
paragraphs.zh: 關鍵是：更好的工作，能否在組織中更容易重複發生。

quote.en: The change is in mechanisms, organization, and work processes, not merely in buying tools.
quote.zh: 轉型的改變在機制、組織與工作流程，不只是購買工具。

source.en: Fate, internal AI transformation kickoff, October 16, 2026, section 2.
source.zh: Fate，2026-10-16 AI 轉型啟動會紀要，§二「轉型的核心」。

title.en: Start with one task, then expand.
title.zh: 先做好一件事，再逐步推廣。

lede.en: Set the goal and standards, start with a real task, then apply what works to the next one.
lede.zh: 先定目標和標準，從一項具體工作開始，做成後再用到下一項工作。

paragraphs.en: People need a shared purpose and clear boundaries. Detailed methods can develop through real tasks and feedback.
paragraphs.zh: 人需要共同目的和清楚邊界，具體做法則可以在真實工作與反饋中形成。

paragraphs.en: An early plan should create room for learning, rather than pretend every useful application is already known.
paragraphs.zh: 早期規劃應為學習留出空間，而不是假設所有有用場景都已經知道。

paragraphs.en: My path began with personal materials. It then grew into working methods, departmental coordination, and a broader company ambition.
paragraphs.zh: 我的路徑從整理個人材料開始，逐步長成工作方法、部門協作，再走向公司層面的目標。

paragraphs.en: Each completed task revealed another problem worth solving. That is how the scope gradually expanded.
paragraphs.zh: 每做成一項工作，就發現下一個值得解決的問題，範圍因此逐步擴大。

paragraphs.en: Departmental work followed the same idea: agree on a baseline, then improve the work as new evidence arrives.
paragraphs.zh: 部門工作的做法也一樣：先確認工作基線，再隨新證據不斷改進。

paragraphs.en: A useful method needs evidence that it helps. When circumstances change, the method should be open to revision.
paragraphs.zh: 方法是否有用，需要實踐證據。情況變化時，方法也應允許修正。

paragraphs.en: I would expand only after the first task has a clear use and people can review its results.
paragraphs.zh: 我會先看第一項工作是否有明確用途、結果能否被人檢視，再決定如何擴展。

quote.en: Start with a real business task. Set direction and standards, then expand after the process works.
quote.zh: 由真正在做業務的人從小事起步，負責人提供方向與標準，跑通後再擴展。

source.en: Fate, internal AI transformation kickoff, October 16, 2026, sections 1.2 and 2.
source.zh: Fate，2026-10-16 AI 轉型啟動會紀要，§1.2 及§二。

title.en: A polished output still needs a purpose.
title.zh: 產出再漂亮，也要有人因此改變行動。

lede.en: The value of AI output depends on what happens because of it.
lede.zh: AI 產出的價值，要看它讓什麼事情發生了變化。

paragraphs.en: Documents, summaries, and dashboards are visible. Their number can grow without making a decision easier or a task better.
paragraphs.zh: 文檔、摘要、看板都很容易被看見，數量增加卻未必讓決策更容易、工作更好。

paragraphs.en: I want to know who uses a result, what they do with it, and what improves afterward.
paragraphs.zh: 我想知道誰在使用成果、用它做什麼，以及之後改善了什麼。

title.en: A reader is not always the destination

paragraphs.en: Some outputs support another process rather than a person reading every word. They still need a clear role and quality standard.
paragraphs.zh: 有些產出是供下一個環節使用，未必需要人逐字閱讀，但仍要有清楚用途與品質標準。

paragraphs.en: Producing more material for people to inspect can simply move the workload instead of reducing it.
paragraphs.zh: 把更多材料交給人檢查，可能只是轉移工作量，而不是減輕負擔。

paragraphs.en: If an output has no useful destination, revise it, combine it, or consider stopping it.
paragraphs.zh: 如果產出找不到有價值的去處，就應考慮調整、合併，或停止。

quote.en: I know AI will generate a pile of junk. I do not want junk.
quote.zh: 我知道 AI 会生成一堆垃圾，我不想要垃圾。

source.en: Fate, operations and innovation meeting, August 25, 2026, section 5: AI work loops.
source.zh: Fate，2026-08-25 運營會＋創新會紀要，§五「AI 閉環建設」，Fate 的回應。

title.zh: 管理，是把工作定義清楚。

lede.en: AI makes unclear goals and acceptance standards harder to ignore.
lede.zh: AI 讓模糊的目標與驗收標準更難被忽略。

title.zh: 一句要求裡，藏著很多取捨

paragraphs.en: A task can sound clear while leaving its scope, evidence requirements, and quality threshold unstated.
paragraphs.zh: 一項任務聽起來很清楚，範圍、證據要求與品質門檻卻可能仍未說明。

paragraphs.en: When those choices remain implicit, the result depends on someone guessing correctly.
paragraphs.zh: 這些取捨如果一直隱含著，結果就依賴別人猜得對不對。

paragraphs.en: For a recurring report, a request for a summary is not enough. Its audience, inputs, and review standard matter too.
paragraphs.zh: 例如一份重複報告，只說「整理摘要」還不夠；給誰看、依據什麼材料、怎樣審閱，同樣需要定義。

paragraphs.en: Explain the purpose, constraints, and acceptance conditions. Record the reasoning that another person needs to continue.
paragraphs.zh: 說清目的、限制與驗收條件，記下下一個人接續工作需要理解的理由。

paragraphs.en: This is management work. AI creates a stronger reason to do it well.
paragraphs.zh: 這本身就是管理工作，而 AI 讓做好它變得更重要。

paragraphs.en: A work instruction puts those choices where people and AI can use them again. It should change when the work changes.
paragraphs.zh: 工作說明書把這些取捨留下來，讓人與 AI 都能再次使用；工作變了，說明也要跟著變。

title.zh: 既要定義 AI 做什麼，也要定義人接下來做什麼

paragraphs.en: A useful instruction connects AI output to the person who will act on it. Otherwise, work can stop at another report.
paragraphs.zh: 一份有用的工作說明書，要把 AI 的產出接到人的下一步行動。只說怎樣生成結果，工作仍可能停在多一份報告。

paragraphs.en: In partner assessment, AI maintains evidence and judgments. People advance conversations, obtain feedback, coordinate resources, and make trade-offs.
paragraphs.zh: 例如伙伴評估：AI 持續整理證據、更新評估；人推動溝通、爭取反饋、協調資源並作出取捨。

paragraphs.en: Clear responsibilities give people more attention for actions that advance the business. Individual speed is only part of the value.
paragraphs.zh: 清晰的分工，讓人能把注意力投入推動業務的行動。個人做得更快只是部分價值，工作能否繼續向前才是關鍵。

title.zh: 讓團隊按共同標準工作

paragraphs.zh: 「時刻注意定義和維護工作說明書，思考每一項工作的標準，不能再依賴每個人各自為戰了。」
paragraphs.en: “Keep defining and maintaining work instructions. Consider standards for every task, instead of relying on everyone working independently.”
Fate, departmental work chat, November 9, 2026, 11:48.

paragraphs.zh: 工作說明書的價值也在於協作：讓不同人和 AI 對同一項工作的要求有共同理解，並把發現的問題修進大家共同使用的方法。
paragraphs.en: Instructions also support collaboration. People and AI share expectations, and lessons improve the method everyone uses.
Clear definitions help execution. People still choose the priorities, resolve trade-offs, and accept the consequences.
paragraphs.zh: 清楚定義有助執行；優先順序、重要取捨及其後果，仍由人負責。

quote.en: The core work shifts from doing each task to defining how each task should be done.
quote.zh: 核心工作從做具體的活，轉向定義每項活怎麼幹。

source.en: Fate, product department meeting, October 20–21, 2026, topic 2: work instructions.
source.zh: Fate，2026-10-20—21 產品部門會紀要，議題二「工作說明書」。

title.en: Knowing what matters becomes more valuable.
title.zh: 更稀缺的，是知道該做什麼。

lede.en: Execution support increases the importance of choosing a worthwhile question.
lede.zh: 執行能力被放大之後，選對問題變得更重要。

title.en: Activity does not choose a direction
title.zh: 忙碌不會自動選出方向

paragraphs.en: Faster production does not tell us which question deserves attention. Judgment decides what evidence is needed and what can wait.
paragraphs.zh: 更快產出，不會自動告訴我們哪個問題值得關注。判斷決定需要什麼證據、哪些事情可以等待。

title.en: Be willing to challenge the story

paragraphs.en: An attractive explanation needs comparison and alternative hypotheses. The useful result may be a narrower conclusion than we expected.
paragraphs.zh: 有吸引力的解釋，需要比較與替代假設。真正有用的結果，可能是比預期更克制的結論。

paragraphs.en: I treat analysis as a way to strengthen judgment, including when it changes my original view.
paragraphs.zh: 我把分析當成加強判斷的方法，包括它推翻我原來想法的時候。

paragraphs.en: Learn to state the problem, identify missing evidence, and explain why the answer would change an action.
paragraphs.zh: 練習說清問題、辨認缺失證據，以及解釋答案會如何改變行動。

quote.en: People define the requirements, make confirmations, and expand and manage their boundaries.
quote.zh: 人負責輸出需求、做確認，並拓展和管理邊界。

source.en: Fate, product department meeting, August 13, 2026, topic 2: boundaries between people and AI.
source.zh: Fate，2026-08-13 產品部門周會紀要，議題二「AI 時代的人機邊界」。

lede.en: A new way of working needs to help people with work they actually face.
lede.zh: 新的工作方式，要能幫人處理眼前真實的工作。

paragraphs.en: A first experiment should help someone finish work they already need to do. Its benefit should be recognizable to that person.
paragraphs.zh: 第一個試驗，應該幫一個人完成本來就需要完成的工作，而且他能感受到其中的幫助。

paragraphs.en: Another report about using AI can become an extra task unless it replaces something less useful.
paragraphs.zh: 如果沒有替代低價值工作，多一份「使用 AI 的報告」可能只是增加一項任務。

paragraphs.en: Time spent checking, correcting, and moving results belongs in the evaluation. A faster draft alone is not the whole outcome.
paragraphs.zh: 檢查、糾錯與轉交成果所花的時間，也應納入評估。初稿更快，不是全部結果。

title.en: Give people a reason to continue

paragraphs.en: A useful result creates trust. Shared standards make that result easier to repeat and improve.
paragraphs.zh: 有用的結果建立信任，共同標準則讓結果更容易重複與改善。

paragraphs.en: I start with a task that helps someone, then use the result to decide what to try next.
paragraphs.zh: 我會先找一件能幫到人的工作，再根據結果決定下一步做什麼。

title.en: Give each side the right work
title.zh: 讓人與 AI 各自做好擅長的工作

paragraphs.en: In partner assessment, AI maintains evidence and judgments. People advance conversations, resolve trade-offs, and decide what happens next.
paragraphs.zh: 在伙伴評估中，AI 持續整理證據、更新判斷；人推動溝通、處理取捨，決定下一步。

paragraphs.en: Relief comes from handing over ongoing work, while giving people room to focus on actions that matter.
paragraphs.zh: 真正的解放，是把持續性的工作交出去，讓人有精力推動重要的事情。清晰的分工，讓 AI 的持續處理能力和人的判斷、關係與行動互相補充。

quote.en: The test is whether this creates more work for people. The goal is to reduce time spent, not increase it.
quote.zh: 判斷標準是有沒有讓大家更累；目標是減少時間消耗，而不是增加。

source.en: Fate, product department meeting, August 13, 2026, topic 1: departmental work management.
source.zh: Fate，2026-08-13 產品部門周會紀要，議題一結論。

title.en: What I did at each stage.
title.zh: 每個階段，我做了哪些事。

lede.en: A monthly record of knowledge-base work, departmental changes, and company-wide AI transformation.
lede.zh: 按月份記錄知識庫整理、部門工作改變，以及公司 AI 轉型的進展。

title.en: Improved continuity between personal and team AI work
title.zh: 完善個人與團隊之間的 AI 工作交接

text.en: Aligned shared facts, working standards, and responsibilities so ongoing work can continue from consistent records.
text.zh: 對齊共同事實、工作標準與責任分工，讓持續工作能從一致的記錄接續。

title.en: Extended AI research to real devices
title.zh: 將 AI 產品調研推進到真機操作

text.en: Tested accessible mobile product flows and captured evidence to compare actual behavior with product documentation.
text.zh: 操作手機上可測的產品流程，保存實測證據，對照官方說明與用戶實際體驗。

title.zh: 為團隊建立共同的業務事實來源

text.en: Published shared factual records and a common reading entry point for research, reports, and collaboration.
text.zh: 建立共同事實記錄與閱讀入口，供研究、報告及協作引用同一套業務事實。

title.en: Standardized partner assessment and moved it onto the AI platform
title.zh: 將伙伴評估標準化，交由 AI 中台持續運行

text.en: A shared framework now supports ongoing assessment updates. People focus on advancing cooperation and making consequential decisions.
text.zh: 完成跨領域伙伴評估框架與人機分工，遷入 AI 中台持續更新評估；同事專注推動合作，並負責重要取捨。

text.en: Consolidated meeting materials while preserving originals and subject references.
text.zh: 集中整理會議材料，保留原件與業務主題的引用。

title.zh: 建立部門 AI 中台，逐步承接通用工作
title.en: Established a departmental AI platform for shared workflows

text.zh: 確立統一的部門工作平台，將已驗證的通用工作按說明書逐步交給 AI 執行；人負責定義、監測與升級。
text.en: Established a shared work platform to take on proven workflows. People define instructions, monitor execution, and improve the methods.

title.zh: 把工作寫成可交接的說明

text.en: Prepared a recurring-report work instruction and supporting handover materials.
text.zh: 形成重複報告工作的說明書與配套交接材料。

text.en: The internal launch brought departmental experience into a wider company transformation effort.
text.zh: 內部啟動把部門經驗帶入更大範圍的公司轉型工作。

title.zh: 準備公司內部轉型分享

text.en: Adapted the transformation material for an internal launch discussion.
text.zh: 將轉型經驗整理為內部啟動討論的分享材料。

title.zh: 讓知識不依附單一工具

text.en: Organized instructions and knowledge for continuity across AI tools.
text.zh: 整理跨 AI 工具接續所需的指令與知識。

text.en: Consolidated research and product material around clearer reading paths.

lede.en: Ray Dalio · My rating: 9.5 / 10
lede.zh: 瑞・達利歐 · 我的評分：9.5 / 10

book_intro.en: Ray Dalio shares the principles he developed through life and work. He explores how reflection, transparency, and clear decision-making can help people and organizations improve.
book_intro.zh: 瑞・達利歐分享他在生活與工作中逐漸形成的原則。這本書探討如何透過反思、透明和清晰的決策，讓個人與組織持續進步。

paragraphs.en: Ray Dalio shares the principles he developed through life and work. He explores how reflection, transparency, and clear decision-making can help people and organizations improve.
paragraphs.zh: 瑞・達利歐分享他在生活與工作中逐漸形成的原則。這本書探討如何透過反思、透明和清晰的決策，讓個人與組織持續進步。

paragraphs.en: Long before AI, Dalio built and managed a company around transparent, structured principles. He applied them to both work and life.
paragraphs.zh: 在沒有 AI 的年代，達利歐就用透明、程序化、結構化的原則建立和管理公司，並把它們貫徹到工作與生活中。

paragraphs.en: Many people have similar ideas, but turning them into a working organization is rare. That ability to make principles real is what I admire most.
paragraphs.zh: 有這類想法的人不少，真正能把原則落實，並據此建立一家有規模的企業，卻很少見。這種把想法變成現實的能力，讓我非常佩服。

paragraphs.en: I consider Principles an essential guide to AI transformation. If knowledge, experience, and processes are already structured, moving them to AI becomes much easier.
paragraphs.zh: 我認為《原則》是指導 AI 轉型的最佳工具書。當知識、經驗和流程已經被梳理成清晰的原則，將它們遷移到 AI 上就會容易得多。

paragraphs.en: Before reading it, I already valued radical transparency, truth, and continuous self-correction. I held myself and my team to the same standards.
paragraphs.zh: 讀這本書之前，我就本能地追求極度透明、極度求真、持續自我迭代，也經常否定自己。無論對自己還是對所管理的團隊，我都走在這條路上。

paragraphs.en: That approach was often painful because many organizations and colleagues did not think it could work. The book gave my instincts a complete framework.
paragraphs.zh: 這樣做時常讓我感到痛苦：這套方法在很多組織裡格格不入，也不容易被認為是可行的。這本書第一次讓我的直覺有了完整的框架。

paragraphs.en: It strengthened my confidence that this path works. My team and I have felt its value in the AI era. I strongly recommend it to anyone pursuing AI transformation.
paragraphs.zh: 它讓我更加確信這條路走得通。我和團隊已經在 AI 時代感受到按這些原則行事的價值，因此強烈推薦給所有正在考慮或推動 AI 轉型的人。

book_intro.en: Jared Diamond asks why societies followed different historical paths. He traces the influence of geography, food production, technology, and disease.
book_intro.zh: 賈雷德・戴蒙德探討不同社會為何走上不同的歷史道路。他從地理、糧食生產、技術和疾病出發，追溯文明發展的深層原因。

paragraphs.en: Jared Diamond asks why societies followed different historical paths. He traces the influence of geography, food production, technology, and disease.
paragraphs.zh: 賈雷德・戴蒙德探討不同社會為何走上不同的歷史道路。他從地理、糧食生產、技術和疾病出發，追溯文明發展的深層原因。

paragraphs.en: I agree with most of the book’s central ideas. It gives a detailed account of how geography shapes the broad direction of history.
paragraphs.zh: 我非常認同這本書的大部分核心觀點。它把時間尺度拉長，從地理與環境出發，詳細解釋了人類歷史為什麼會走向不同的方向。

paragraphs.en: If history began again, I think much of the same pattern would probably recur. Among books with this perspective, this is the most complete account I have read.
paragraphs.zh: 順著這個邏輯推想：如果人類歷史重來一次，大概率還會重演類似的劇本。持這種視角的書並不少，但這一本講得最完整、最詳盡，我也認為它的結論大概率是對的。

paragraphs.en: I find the framework useful for organizations too. Their initial resources and founders’ backgrounds can shape how far they can go.
paragraphs.zh: 我認為這套框架也能用來理解商業和組織：創立時擁有的核心資源，以及創始人的背景，很大程度上會影響一家企業能走多遠。

paragraphs.en: Large companies are hard to displace, yet innovation often emerges elsewhere. I see a similar pattern in the history described here.
paragraphs.zh: 大企業雖然很難倒下，創新卻往往不從巨頭內部長出來；我在這裡看到了與人類歷史相似的規律。

paragraphs.en: The same applies to personal growth. Family, environment, and the complexity of experience can profoundly influence a person’s path.
paragraphs.zh: 個人成長也是一樣：家庭背景、成長環境和經歷的複雜度，都會在很大程度上影響一個人未來的高度。

paragraphs.en: Its arguments about European fragmentation and the role of writing and language also stayed with me.
paragraphs.zh: 書中關於歐洲的成功與長期分裂之間的關係，以及文字、語言在文明演化中的作用，也都值得反覆思考。

book_intro.en: Scott Anderson follows four people through the Middle East during World War I. Their stories reveal how war and competing ambitions shaped the modern region.

paragraphs.en: Scott Anderson follows four people through the Middle East during World War I. Their stories reveal how war and competing ambitions shaped the modern region.
paragraphs.zh: 斯科特・安德森以四個人的經歷，串起第一次世界大戰中的中東。戰爭、列強的交易與彼此衝突的理想，共同塑造了現代中東的輪廓。

paragraphs.en: This book helped me understand how wartime promises and bargains shaped the modern Middle East.
paragraphs.zh: 這本書第一次讓我更清楚地理解現代中東是如何被塑造出來的。

paragraphs.en: British promises, the Sykes–Picot Agreement, and the Balfour Declaration formed overlapping commitments. Their consequences helped shape the region’s later history.
paragraphs.zh: 麥克馬洪的許諾、《賽克斯—皮科協定》和《貝爾福宣言》等承諾與交易層層交疊，逐步塑造了後來的中東格局。

paragraphs.en: What moved me most was how ordinary people in Western powers saw themselves and the world. Many believed they could change it.
paragraphs.zh: 最打動我的是，書中那些英國等西方列強的普通人如何看待自己和世界：他們充滿自信，相信自己能改變世界。

paragraphs.en: That sense of mission came at a personal cost. Families could spend decades apart as people traveled to distant imperial outposts.
paragraphs.zh: 但這種改天換地的使命感也有代價：人們遠赴帝國的前哨，許多家庭長年離散，有的甚至大半生無法團聚。

paragraphs.en: I was struck by how idealism could gradually give way to disillusionment. The contrast between historical attitudes toward Western powers and those I see today also stayed with me.
paragraphs.zh: 理想主義在具體執行中一步步幻滅，也讓我印象深刻。當時部分中東人對西方的期待，與我今天看到的態度形成反差，這種歷史的回聲值得反覆琢磨。

lede.en: Daniel Gordis · My rating: 8.5 / 10
lede.zh: 丹尼爾・戈迪斯 · 我的評分：8.5 / 10

book_intro.en: Daniel Gordis traces the modern history of the Jewish people and the State of Israel. He follows the ideas, conflicts, and choices that shaped the nation.
book_intro.zh: 丹尼爾・戈迪斯梳理近現代猶太人與以色列的歷史。從思想的興起到建國後的衝突與抉擇，書中呈現了一個國家的形成與發展。

paragraphs.en: Daniel Gordis traces the modern history of the Jewish people and the State of Israel. He follows the ideas, conflicts, and choices that shaped the nation.
paragraphs.zh: 丹尼爾・戈迪斯梳理近現代猶太人與以色列的歷史。從思想的興起到建國後的衝突與抉擇，書中呈現了一個國家的形成與發展。

paragraphs.en: This is a clear, accessible history with a remarkable amount of information. It reads like a history textbook without feeling difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 這本書像一本通俗易懂的歷史課本：信息量很大，歷史脈絡卻非常清晰，讀起來並不費力。

paragraphs.en: As a Chinese reader, I had few opportunities to understand Israel in depth. This book let me see its modern history from a Jewish perspective.
paragraphs.zh: 作為中國人，我此前很少有機會深入了解以色列。這本書讓我第一次得以從猶太人的視角，較完整地審視它從建國到今天的歷程。

paragraphs.en: I admire what people achieved with limited resources under difficult conditions. Their experience reminds me of another people who have endured and worked through hardship.
paragraphs.zh: 我佩服這個民族在有限資源和重重困境下取得的成就。這也讓我想到中國人同樣在苦難中奮鬥的經歷。

paragraphs.en: I do not want to reduce history to a simple judgment of right and wrong. The same events look different from different perspectives.
paragraphs.zh: 我不想把歷史簡單歸結為對錯。同一段歷史從不同視角看，呈現的樣貌必然不同；我也希望有一天讀到阿拉伯視角的相關歷史。

paragraphs.en: The book also challenged my assumptions about relationships with Western countries. It made me appreciate the difficult choices faced by a small country.
paragraphs.zh: 書中也糾正了我不少認知盲區，包括以色列與西方國家的關係並非始終順遂。它讓我更深刻地感受到小國在複雜處境中的生存壓力。

paragraphs.en: My most important takeaway is that environments shape nations and people. Growth through adversity can also be a trait of resilient organizations and individuals.
paragraphs.zh: 最重要的體會是：環境造就民族，也造就人。在逆境中成長，往往也是有韌性的組織與個人的共同點。

book_intro.en: Phil Champagne collects Satoshi Nakamoto’s writings and early discussions about Bitcoin. The book follows its ideas and development through the creator’s own words.
book_intro.zh: 菲爾・尚帕涅編集了中本聰的文字與早期討論。讀者可以從創造者的文字中，看到比特幣的理念與發展過程。

paragraphs.en: Phil Champagne collects Satoshi Nakamoto’s writings and early discussions about Bitcoin. The book follows its ideas and development through the creator’s own words.
paragraphs.zh: 菲爾・尚帕涅編集了中本聰的文字與早期討論。讀者可以從創造者的文字中，看到比特幣的理念與發展過程。

paragraphs.en: For anyone interested in crypto, I believe the Bitcoin white paper is essential reading. I see this collection as a companion to it.
paragraphs.zh: 我認為，對加密領域的從業者和愛好者來說，比特幣白皮書是必讀的。這本文集則可以看作白皮書的延伸閱讀。

paragraphs.en: It gathers Satoshi Nakamoto’s posts and discussions, showing how Bitcoin’s ideas were put into practice.
paragraphs.zh: 它把中本聰散落在網絡各處的文字編集起來，記錄了比特幣的理念如何一步步付諸實踐。

paragraphs.en: My biggest takeaway is that Bitcoin did not appear fully formed. It began with an extraordinary design and grew through many people’s contributions.
paragraphs.zh: 我最大的收穫是看清比特幣並非一蹴而就：它來自一個天才頭腦和出色的初始設計，也來自許多人持續的完善與進步。

paragraphs.en: The early discussions, disagreements, and fixes are part of its history. They show how a community helped an idea develop.
paragraphs.zh: 早期論壇中的討論、爭論和修補，本身就是比特幣誕生史的一部分。

paragraphs.en: I have seen many criticisms about mining, resource use, and Bitcoin’s value. The collection preserves early answers and reasoning behind those questions.
paragraphs.zh: 我見過很多人質疑挖礦的意義、資源消耗和比特幣的價值。書中保留了對這些問題的早期思考與回答，值得回到原始討論中閱讀。

paragraphs.en: If you have read the white paper and want to understand Bitcoin’s origins, this book is worth reading. Some technical background helps.
paragraphs.zh: 如果讀過白皮書後還想了解比特幣的起源，這本書值得一讀；有一點技術背景會更容易理解。

book_quotes.original: 比特币是一种使用密码技术以及分布式网络替代中央可信服务器的数字货币

lede.en: Ari Shavit · My rating: 8.5 / 10

book_intro.en: Journalist Ari Shavit tells Israel’s story through family history, interviews, and individual lives. His account explores both the country’s achievements and its tragedies.
book_intro.zh: 記者阿里・沙維特通過家族故事、訪談與個人經歷講述以色列的歷史。這本書既寫國家的成就，也直面其中的悲劇與矛盾。

paragraphs.en: Journalist Ari Shavit tells Israel’s story through family history, interviews, and individual lives. His account explores both the country’s achievements and its tragedies.
paragraphs.zh: 記者阿里・沙維特通過家族故事、訪談與個人經歷講述以色列的歷史。這本書既寫國家的成就，也直面其中的悲劇與矛盾。

paragraphs.en: Compared with the more detached Israel, this book is emotional and openly takes a position. I found it hard to put down.
paragraphs.zh: 與冷靜的《以色列：一個民族的重生》相比，這本書更有感情、更有立場，甚至有點煽動；但它也更好看，讓我讀得停不下來。

paragraphs.en: The author comes from a Zionist family, so his perspective is part of the story. His journalism also makes room for difficult questions.
paragraphs.zh: 作者出身於復國主義精英家庭，有自己的立場很正常；這恰恰也是理解這段歷史需要的一個視角。難得的是，他的記者身份讓他沒有一味只講一方的對錯。

paragraphs.en: My strongest impression is that both sides have their own suffering and reasons. Understanding their experiences requires changing perspectives.
paragraphs.zh: 讀完最大的感受是：換位去看，雙方都有自己的苦難和道理。至於誰對誰錯，或許永遠不會有一個簡單答案。

paragraphs.en: I also admire the country’s resilience. To me, strength is not something a people are born with; hardship can shape it.
paragraphs.zh: 拋開對錯，我依然佩服這個國家在困境中的韌性。我認為沒有天生強大的民族，很多強大是在苦難中被塑造出來的。

paragraphs.en: Another thought stayed with me: struggle can make you resemble your enemy. Survival may lead people to do things they once could not imagine.
paragraphs.zh: 另一個印象最深的體會是：鬥爭可能讓你越來越像你的敵人。為了活下去，人可能會做出自己從前絕不會做的事；國家、組織和個人都可能面對這樣的處境。

paragraphs.en: I recommend reading Israel first for the historical background. Then read this book to see how major events affected ordinary lives.
paragraphs.zh: 我建議先讀《以色列》補全歷史脈絡，再讀這本書，看看大時代中的事件如何落到一個個普通人身上。

title.en: Why Nations Fail: The Origins of Power, Prosperity and Poverty

lede.en: Daron Acemoglu & James A. Robinson · My rating: 9 / 10
lede.zh: 德隆・阿西莫格魯 / 詹姆斯・A. 羅賓遜 · 我的評分：9 / 10

author.zh: 德隆・阿西莫格魯、詹姆斯・A. 羅賓遜

book_intro.en: Institutional economics at its best. Rich nations differ from poor ones not by geography or culture, but by inclusive versus extractive institutions.
book_intro.zh: 制度經濟學代表作：國家間的貧富差距不在地理或文化，而在包容性制度與汲取性制度之分。

paragraphs.en: Why are some nations rich and others poor? The authors answer with one word: institutions. Inclusive systems spread power and reward innovation. Extractive ones let a few live off the many.
paragraphs.zh: 為什麼有的國家富、有的國家窮？作者的答案是制度。包容性制度分散權力、獎勵創新；汲取性制度讓少數人靠多數人過活。

paragraphs.en: The proof is a sweep of world history: from the two Nogales to the Black Death. Then on to the Glorious Revolution and the Industrial Revolution.
paragraphs.zh: 論證材料是一整部世界史：從諾加利斯同城兩岸，到黑死病、光榮革命與工業革命。

paragraphs.en: If you want a way to predict the future, you will be disappointed: the authors insist history turns on contingency. But as an explanation of history, it is convincing.
paragraphs.zh: 想從中找到預測未來的公式，你會失望：作者強調歷史轉折充滿偶然。但作為對歷史的解釋，它令人信服。

paragraphs.en: Reading it feels like reading the history of world civilization. You come away understanding why the world looks the way it does today.
paragraphs.zh: 讀它相當於讀了一整部世界文明史。讀完你會明白，當今世界為什麼是現在這個樣子。

paragraphs.en: It pairs well with Guns, Germs, and Steel: one explains history by geography, this one by institutions.
paragraphs.zh: 它與《槍炮、病菌與鋼鐵》正好構成對照：一本用地理解釋歷史，一本用制度解釋歷史。

book_quotes.original: 是自由让世界富裕。
book_quotes.translation: It is freedom that makes the world rich.

source.en: Why Nations Fail · Institutions and prosperity
source.zh: 《國家為什麼會失敗》· 制度與繁榮

book_quotes.original: 关键是经济增长能否持续，能否实现长期经济增长，只有包容性制度才能够实现长期经济增长
book_quotes.translation: What matters is whether growth can last. Only inclusive institutions can sustain growth over the long run.

source.en: Why Nations Fail · Inclusive institutions
source.zh: 《國家為什麼會失敗》· 包容性制度

book_quotes.original: 包容性制度的建立具有偶然性
book_quotes.translation: The rise of inclusive institutions is a matter of contingency.

source.en: Why Nations Fail · History and contingency
source.zh: 《國家為什麼會失敗》· 歷史與偶然

book_quotes.original: 对创造性破坏的担心是造成新石器革命和工业革命之间生活水平没有持续提高的主要原因。
book_quotes.translation: Fear of creative destruction is the main reason living standards did not keep rising between the Neolithic and Industrial Revolutions.

source.en: Why Nations Fail · Creative destruction
source.zh: 《國家為什麼會失敗》· 創造性破壞

book_quotes.original: 像英国、美国这些国家之所以富裕是因为他们的人民推翻了控制权力的精英，并创造出了政治权力广泛分散的社会
book_quotes.translation: Countries like Britain and America grew rich because their people overturned ruling elites and built societies with widely dispersed political power.

source.en: Why Nations Fail · Critical junctures
source.zh: 《國家為什麼會失敗》· 關鍵節點

lede.en: Adam Smith · My rating: 9 / 10
lede.zh: 亞當・斯密 · 我的評分：9 / 10

book_intro.en: The founding work of economics, published in 1776: labor, division of work, prices, and the invisible hand. I read it abridged, not in full.
book_intro.zh: 1776 年問世的經濟學奠基之作：勞動、分工、價格與看不見的手。我讀的是節選，非全本。

paragraphs.en: Everyone has heard of it; almost no one has read it. The world has changed beyond recognition in 250 years, yet so many core principles here still hold.
paragraphs.zh: 人人都聽說過它，卻幾乎沒人真正讀過它。250 年間世界早已改頭換面，但書中如此多的核心原則至今依然成立。

paragraphs.en: The nature of wealth, the division of labor, the invisible hand, free markets, capital and profit. My abridged reading covered the five core books, ending on taxes.
paragraphs.zh: 財富的本質、分工、看不見的手、自由市場、資本與利潤。我的節選覆蓋五篇核心，止於賦稅。

paragraphs.en: If you want to be rational, objective, and able to think independently, this is required reading. The core ideas cannot be overemphasized.
paragraphs.zh: 想成為理性、客觀、有獨立思考能力的人，這是必讀書目。這些核心思想怎麼強調都不為過。

paragraphs.en: Smith wrote in the early days of central bank money. So his account of how money emerges is vivid and full of detail.
paragraphs.zh: 斯密親歷央行發行貨幣的早期時代，所以他對貨幣起源的描述格外有畫面感、細節豐富。

paragraphs.en: The later parts on taxes and land rent are dry and dated. Even so, the first half alone is enough.
paragraphs.zh: 後半部分論稅收與地租較為晦澀，且與如今情況差異較大；但即使只讀前半部分，也足夠起作用了。

book_quotes.original: 使用价值很大的东西，往往交换价值极小，甚至没有；反之，交换价值很大的东西，亦往往使用价值极小，甚至没有。
book_quotes.translation: Things with great value in use often have little or no value in exchange; and things with great value in exchange often have little or no value in use.

source.en: The Wealth of Nations · Book I · Value in use and in exchange
source.zh: 《國富論》· 第一篇 · 使用價值與交換價值

book_quotes.original: 所有人都成了商人，而社会也渐渐成为所谓的商业社会。
book_quotes.translation: When everyone becomes a trader, society itself becomes what we call a commercial society.

source.en: The Wealth of Nations · Book I · The origin of money
source.zh: 《國富論》· 第一篇 · 論貨幣的起源

book_quotes.original: 社会财富、国民财富和私人财富能够得以产生的重要因素是每个人改善自身状况的共同的、经常的、不懈的努力。
book_quotes.translation: The wealth of society and of individuals arises from the constant, universal effort of every person to better their own condition.

source.en: The Wealth of Nations · Book II · On capital
source.zh: 《國富論》· 第二篇 · 論資本

book_quotes.original: 所有铸币的价值都由其中最贵重的那种金属的价值来支配。
book_quotes.translation: The value of all coinage is governed by the value of the dearest metal among them.

source.en: The Wealth of Nations · Book I · The value of coinage
source.zh: 《國富論》· 第一篇 · 鑄幣的價值

book_quotes.original: 中产及富有阶级的人如果真的明白自己的利益，就应该反对对生活必需品征税，反对对劳动工资直接征税。
book_quotes.translation: The middle classes and the rich, if they understood their own interest, would oppose taxes on necessities and on the wages of labor.

source.en: The Wealth of Nations · Book V · On taxes
source.zh: 《國富論》· 第五篇 · 論賦稅

title.en: Layered Money: From Gold and Dollars to Bitcoin and Central Bank Digital Currencies

lede.en: Nik Bhatia · My rating: 8 / 10
lede.zh: 尼克・巴蒂亞 · 我的評分：8 / 10

book_intro.en: A short history of money through one lens: layered hierarchy. First-layer money has no counterparty; second-layer money is a promise that can default.
book_intro.zh: 用「分層」框架讀通整部貨幣史：第一層貨幣沒有交易對手方，第二層貨幣是可能違約的承諾。

paragraphs.en: The author traces money from Florentine florins and bills of exchange, through the gold standard and the dollar. He ends with Bitcoin and central bank digital currencies.
paragraphs.zh: 作者從佛羅倫薩弗羅林與匯票講起，經金本位與美元，一直講到比特幣與央行數字貨幣。

paragraphs.en: His central claim is controversial: Bitcoin will become the only first-layer money, sitting at the top of the pyramid.
paragraphs.zh: 他的核心論點爭議很大：比特幣將成為唯一的第一層貨幣，站在金字塔尖。

paragraphs.en: I work in crypto, and I side with the author. This book gave me a framework to place that view. Money is layered, and first-layer money is the money of money.
paragraphs.zh: 我是加密從業者，傾向於認可作者的觀點。這本書給了我安放這個觀點的框架：貨幣是分層的，第一層貨幣就是貨幣的貨幣。

paragraphs.en: Many scholars disagree, arguing Bitcoin is too volatile and has no state backing. Reading both sides is exactly why this book is worth your time.
paragraphs.zh: 很多學者不買賬，認為比特幣波動太大、沒有國家背書。把兩邊論點都讀一遍，正是這本書的價值所在。

paragraphs.en: Whatever your country or industry, you should understand money. What it is, where it came from, and why it holds value.
paragraphs.zh: 無論什麼國家、什麼行業、什麼背景，人都應該了解錢：它是什麼、從哪裡來、為什麼有價值。

book_quotes.original: 第一层货币是“无交易对手方”的
book_quotes.translation: First-layer money has no counterparty.

source.en: Layered Money · First-layer money
source.zh: 《貨幣金字塔》· 第一層貨幣

book_quotes.original: 第二层货币汇票是一种承诺，有违约的风险。
book_quotes.translation: Second-layer money, like the bill of exchange, is a promise — and promises can default.

source.en: Layered Money · Second-layer money
source.zh: 《貨幣金字塔》· 第二層貨幣

book_quotes.original: 货币不仅具有流通和价值储藏的功能，它还是一种记账单位。
book_quotes.translation: Money is not only a medium of exchange and a store of value — it is also a unit of account.

source.en: Layered Money · The three functions of money
source.zh: 《貨幣金字塔》· 貨幣的三重職能

book_quotes.original: 政府无法抵挡为自己不受约束地创造货币的诱惑。
book_quotes.translation: No government can resist the temptation to create money for itself without restraint.

source.en: Layered Money · Chapter 1 · The debasement of coinage
source.zh: 《貨幣金字塔》· 第一章 · 政府造币的诱惑

book_quotes.original: 比特币是一种不产生于中央银行资产负债表、价值能够自我保证的新资产，它们是银行发行数字现金的储备货币，因而具备成为第一层货币的资格。
book_quotes.translation: Bitcoin is a new asset born outside central bank balance sheets, with value that guarantees itself — qualifying it as reserve money for banks' digital cash, and as first-layer money.

source.en: Layered Money · The Renaissance of money
source.zh: 《貨幣金字塔》· 貨幣的文藝復興

title.en: The Federal Reserve and the Financial Crisis

lede.en: Ben S. Bernanke · My rating: 7.5 / 10
lede.zh: 本・伯南克 · 我的評分：7.5 / 10

book_intro.en: Four lectures by the Fed chair who lived through 2008. Central banking history, the gold standard, the crisis, and unconventional policy.
book_intro.zh: 親歷 2008 危機的美聯儲主席的四次講座：央行史、金本位、危機復盤與非常規政策。

paragraphs.en: Strictly a collection of four public lectures, not a book. Some background in finance and economics helps.
paragraphs.zh: 嚴格說是四次公開講座的合集，不是著作。最好有一點金融和經濟學背景。

paragraphs.en: It covers the birth of central banks and why the gold standard failed. Then how the 2008 crisis unfolded, and how the Fed responded.
paragraphs.zh: 內容覆蓋央行的誕生、金本位為何失敗、2008 危機如何演變，以及美聯儲如何應對。

paragraphs.en: The most valuable part is Bernanke's firsthand account of 2008. Not many authors can write about a crisis from inside the command room.
paragraphs.zh: 最有價值的是伯南克對 2008 的親歷視角。能在危機指揮室內部寫危機的作者，屈指可數。

paragraphs.en: For finance, learning about crises always pays off: it sharpens your vigilance. The last global one was 2008, and there will be more.
paragraphs.zh: 對金融而言，多了解危機總有好處：它能提高你的警惕。上一次席捲全球的是 2008，但不會是最後一次。

book_quotes.original: 根据“白芝浩原则”，缓解金融恐慌的最佳方式就是为那些缺乏资金的机构提供流动性。
book_quotes.translation: By Bagehot's rule, the best way to calm a financial panic is to supply liquidity to institutions that lack funding.

source.en: The Federal Reserve and the Financial Crisis · The lender of last resort
source.zh: 《金融的本質》· 最後貸款人

book_quotes.original: 试图通过货币政策来维持过低的失业率，最终会引发通货膨胀。
book_quotes.translation: Trying to hold unemployment too low through monetary policy will ultimately ignite inflation.

source.en: The Federal Reserve and the Financial Crisis · Lecture 2 · The Fed after WWII
source.zh: 《金融的本質》· 第二講 · 戰後的美聯儲

book_quotes.original: 在金本位制下，经济产出和通胀水平的波动性都更大
book_quotes.translation: Under the gold standard, both output and inflation were more volatile.

source.en: The Federal Reserve and the Financial Crisis · The cost of gold
source.zh: 《金融的本質》· 金本位的代價

book_quotes.original: 真正的金本位制会创造出一个自我管理的货币体系，而这样的货币体系至少能部分替代央行的职能
book_quotes.translation: A true gold standard creates a self-managing monetary system that could partly replace the central bank.

source.en: The Federal Reserve and the Financial Crisis · The gold standard
source.zh: 《金融的本質》· 金本位

book_quotes.original: 伯南克主张设定一个明确的通胀目标，并清晰地向公众传达政策目标和计划行为，以引导市场通胀预期
book_quotes.translation: Bernanke argues for a clear inflation target, communicated openly to the public, to guide market expectations.

source.en: The Federal Reserve and the Financial Crisis · Central bank communication
source.zh: 《金融的本質》· 央行溝通

title.en: The Pay Off: How Changing the Way We Pay Changes Everything

lede.en: Gottfried Leibbrandt & Natasha de Terán · My rating: 9 / 10
lede.zh: 戈特弗里德・萊伯蘭特 / 娜塔莎・德・特蘭 · 我的評分：9 / 10

author.zh: 戈特弗里德・萊伯蘭特、娜塔莎・德・特蘭

book_intro.en: A panoramic biography of payments: money's purpose, card economics, invisible plumbing, and sanctions.
book_intro.zh: 支付體系的全景傳記：從貨幣的本質，到卡的經濟引擎、隱形管道與制裁武器化。

paragraphs.en: Two payment insiders explain how payments really work: where money came from, and how cards and SWIFT move it. They also show who pays for every step.
paragraphs.zh: 兩位支付業內資深人士講解支付究竟如何運轉：貨幣從何而來，卡、清算所與 SWIFT 如何搬動資金，每一步由誰買單。

paragraphs.en: The story runs from London clearing houses to India's UPI, from the four-party card model to sanctions and digital currencies.
paragraphs.zh: 主線從倫敦清算所講到印度 UPI 即時支付，從信用卡四角模式講到制裁武器化與央行數字貨幣。

paragraphs.en: I came to it as a complete outsider who works on payment-related products. It exceeded expectations: clear, fun, and dense with facts. I highlighted nearly every page.
paragraphs.zh: 我是帶著工作裡的疑問入門的門外漢。這本書遠超預期：看得懂，還津津有味，概念與數據密度極高，我幾乎每一頁都做了標註。

paragraphs.en: Payments concern everyone, yet almost nobody understands them. We rarely know what each transaction costs, or how much banks earn from it.
paragraphs.zh: 支付人人相關，卻幾乎沒人真正了解。你不知道自己每天都在為每一筆付費，也不知道銀行從支付裡賺走了多少。

paragraphs.en: As a product person, the key lesson stuck: people do not want to pay. A great payment is invisible—the best payment is no payment at all.
paragraphs.zh: 對做產品的我，最大的啟示是：人們不想支付，只想要支付更方便。好用的支付就是沒有支付。

paragraphs.en: If I had read it earlier, it would have given me a framework for this world much sooner. For a first book on payments, this is the one.
paragraphs.zh: 如果更早讀到，它會幫我更早搭起理解這個世界的框架。要挑一本支付入門書，選它不會錯。

book_quotes.original: 货币的终极目的是使用，即用来支付
book_quotes.translation: The ultimate purpose of money is to use it — to pay.

source.en: The Pay Off · Part I · The purpose of money
source.zh: 《支付的故事》· 第一編 · 貨幣的終極目的

book_quotes.original: 支付系统所能企盼的最大荣誉就是被遗忘。
book_quotes.translation: The greatest honour a payment system can aspire to is to be forgotten.

source.en: The Pay Off · The invisible plumbing
source.zh: 《支付的故事》· 隱形管道

book_quotes.original: 信用卡的费用是由持卡人支付的，但我们认为自己没有支付。
book_quotes.translation: Credit card costs are paid by cardholders, yet we believe we are not paying.

source.en: The Pay Off · The economics of cards
source.zh: 《支付的故事》· 卡的經濟引擎

book_quotes.original: 人们不想进行支付，他们想让支付变得更加方便
book_quotes.translation: People do not want to make payments. They want paying to be more convenient.

source.en: The Pay Off · Seamless payments
source.zh: 《支付的故事》· 無縫支付

book_quotes.original: 支付和货币的核心是信任，或者说，对彼此的信誉缺乏信任——我们不信任彼此，但我们信任这个系统。
book_quotes.translation: The core of payments and money is trust — or rather, a lack of trust in each other. We do not trust each other, but we trust the system.

source.en: The Pay Off · The core of payments is trust
source.zh: 《支付的故事》· 支付的核心是信任

title.en: Paying with Plastic: The Digital Revolution in Buying and Borrowing (Second Edition)

lede.en: David S. Evans & Richard Schmalensee · My rating: 8 / 10
lede.zh: 戴維・S. 埃文斯 / 理查德・斯默蘭 · 我的評分：8 / 10

author.zh: 戴維・S. 埃文斯、理查德・斯默蘭

book_intro.en: An economics classic on the card industry: two-sided markets, co-opetition, interchange fees, and antitrust battles.
book_intro.zh: 支付卡產業的專業之作：以雙邊市場與競合組織兩大理論框架，剖析支付卡的誕生、演變與競爭格局。

paragraphs.en: First published in 1999, this is a deep, focused study of the payment card industry. It runs from the 1950 Diners card to Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Discover.
paragraphs.zh: 1999 年初版的專業著作，聚焦卡支付領域：從 1950 年大萊卡，講到維薩、萬事達、運通與發現卡的競爭格局。

paragraphs.en: Its two analytic pillars are two-sided markets and co-opetition. Card networks balance issuers and merchants, share a platform, and still compete.
paragraphs.zh: 全書以雙邊市場與競合組織兩大框架展開：卡組織如何平衡發卡與收單兩側、共享平台又彼此競爭。

paragraphs.en: It pairs well with The Pay Off: that book is broad, this one goes deep on cards. In the West, cards are the backbone of payments.
paragraphs.zh: 它與《支付的故事》正好互補：那本廣而泛，這本專業且垂直。在西方世界，卡支付就是支付領域最重要的組成部分。

paragraphs.en: Everyday questions get answered here: debit versus credit, how much I actually pay to pay, and what Visa really is.
paragraphs.zh: 普通人的問題讀完都會明白：借記卡和信用卡的區別、我為支付付出了多少費用、VISA 到底是家什麼樣的組織。

paragraphs.en: It is less beginner-friendly: some parts are dense. With a little background in payments first, it takes you one level deeper.
paragraphs.zh: 它不夠新手友好，有些地方略晦澀；先讀過《支付的故事》再讀它，理解會更深一層。

paragraphs.en: The industry direction I took away: cash fades, payments go invisible, and intermediaries shrink. Crypto may be the best tool to push that trend.
paragraphs.zh: 我帶走的行業判斷：現金消亡、無感支付、減少中介都是確定的演變方向，加密也許是推動這個趨勢的最佳工具。

book_quotes.original: 货币不过是记录在没有价值的纸张或金属上的有保证的数字。它最终会演变成一种以微电子和光子形式进行排列的有保证的数据（guaranteed data），并以光速在整个世界流通运转。
book_quotes.translation: Money is nothing but guaranteed numbers recorded on worthless paper or metal. It will become guaranteed data, arranged in electrons and photons, moving around the world at light speed.

source.en: Paying with Plastic · Epigraph by Dee Hock, founder of Visa
source.zh: 《銀行卡時代》· 迪・霍克題辭（維薩創始人）

book_quotes.original: 货币对社会来说并不是免费的，因为它需要消耗资源
book_quotes.translation: Money is not free for society, because it consumes resources.

source.en: Paying with Plastic · The cost of money
source.zh: 《銀行卡時代》· 貨幣的成本

book_quotes.original: 信用交易比原始货币出现得要早
book_quotes.translation: Credit transactions appeared earlier than primitive money.

source.en: Paying with Plastic · Credit before money
source.zh: 《銀行卡時代》· 信用早於貨幣

book_quotes.original: 会员们几乎在其他的每一个方面展开竞争——例如利率、费用、服务以及新型产品的创新方面。这被称为竞合（co-opetition）
book_quotes.translation: Members compete in almost every other respect — rates, fees, services, and innovation. This is called co-opetition.

source.en: Paying with Plastic · Co-opetition
source.zh: 《銀行卡時代》· 競合組織

book_quotes.original: 对大多数人来说，他们最大的资产就是自己本身以及工作和赚钱的能力。
book_quotes.translation: For most people, their greatest asset is themselves — their ability to work and to earn.

source.en: Paying with Plastic · The joys and sorrows of lending
source.zh: 《銀行卡時代》· 放貸的苦與樂

kicker.zh: 案例 09 / 部門 AI 工作平台

title.zh: 搭建 AI 中台，成為統一的部門工作平台。
title.en: Build an AI hub as the shared departmental work platform.

lede.zh: 將已驗證的工作逐步交給部門 AI 中台。AI 負責執行，人負責定義工作、監測結果、升級方法，並拓展下一項工作。
lede.en: Move proven workflows onto a departmental AI platform. AI executes; people define work, monitor results, improve methods, and expand responsibilities.

title.zh: 把一項工作交過去，而不只是放一份結果

paragraphs.zh: 中台逐步承接部門的具體工作。工作說明書、必要材料與執行要求一起交接，讓 AI 能持續完成工作，成果頁面則讓人了解運行結果。
paragraphs.en: The platform gradually takes on departmental tasks. Instructions, required materials, and execution requirements travel together, with results available for review.

paragraphs.zh: 每項工作先定義清楚並完成驗證，再交中台執行。人仍可根據實際效果修改標準，讓下一輪執行沿用改進後的方法。
paragraphs.en: Each workflow is defined and tested before handover. People refine its standards, so subsequent runs use the improved method.

paragraphs.zh: 客服工單日報與伙伴評估已交由中台運行。前者持續整理客服問題，後者根據新反饋與材料更新評估，讓日常維護不再依賴人工逐項追記。
paragraphs.en: Support reporting and partner assessment now run on the platform. They organize support issues and update assessments as evidence arrives.

paragraphs.zh: 伙伴評估的分工尤其清楚：AI 維護評估，人推動溝通與合作。人的行動帶來新資料，AI 再把資料變成更新後的判斷。
paragraphs.en: In partner assessment, AI maintains evaluations while people advance relationships. Their conversations generate new evidence for AI to assess.

title.zh: 人的工作：定義、監測、升級

paragraphs.zh: 人寫清工作目的、輸入、方法、輸出和驗收標準，監測執行是否有效；出現偏差，就調整說明書與工作方式。重要取捨仍由人決定。
paragraphs.en: People define purposes, inputs, methods, outputs, and acceptance standards. They monitor execution, improve instructions, and make consequential decisions.

paragraphs.zh: 一項工作穩定承接之後，人繼續識別值得做的新工作，定義新的說明書，逐步拓展中台可承擔的範圍。
paragraphs.en: Once a workflow is established, people identify valuable new work. New instructions gradually expand what the platform can handle.

paragraphs.zh: 我推動部門從使用 AI 工具轉向建立共同工作平台，明確交接標準與人機分工，並以實際工作檢查這套方式是否有效。
paragraphs.en: I guide the shared work platform, define handover standards, and test responsibilities through real work.

image_alt.zh: 部門 AI 中台首頁

title.zh: AI 接手之後，人要拓展什麼？
title.en: What should people take on after AI takes over?

lede.zh: 把已有工作交給 AI 只是起點。更重要的是，把原來沒能力做、做不好的工作，變成下一步能推動的事。
lede.en: Handing existing work to AI is a starting point. The next question is what people can now accomplish.

quote.zh: 人要輸出需求、做確認，並不斷拓展和管理工作邊界；這是是否真正駕馭 AI 的體現。
quote.en: People define requirements, confirm decisions, and expand their responsibilities. Managing that boundary shows whether they truly direct AI.

source.zh: Fate，2026-08-13 產品部門周會紀要，議題二「AI 時代的人機邊界」。
source.en: Fate, product department meeting, August 13, 2026, topic 2: responsibilities in AI work.

title.zh: 分工要說清楚，也要持續調整

paragraphs.zh: 我關心的分工，是讓 AI 承擔已定義的執行工作，讓人掌握方向、確認關鍵選擇，並尋找下一個值得解決的問題。
paragraphs.en: I want AI to execute defined work. People set direction, confirm consequential choices, and find the next worthwhile problem.

paragraphs.zh: 邊界會隨能力變化。已經驗證有效的方法可以交出去，新的問題與取捨則需要人繼續定義。
paragraphs.en: Responsibilities evolve with capability. Proven methods can be delegated, while people define how to address new problems and trade-offs.

title.zh: 省下的時間，要變成新的業務行動
title.en: Turn saved time into business action

paragraphs.zh: 以伙伴評估為例，AI 接手資料整理和持續更新，人就應把更多精力放到取得反饋、推動合作和解決阻礙上。
paragraphs.en: When AI maintains partner assessments, people can focus on obtaining feedback, advancing cooperation, and resolving obstacles.

paragraphs.zh: 我希望看到的成果，是原來顧不上的機會有人推進，原來做不好的工作有了新的辦法，而不只是個人完成任務更快。
paragraphs.en: I want overlooked opportunities pursued and difficult work handled better. Faster individual task completion is only part of that change.
